title: Post Click Prediction
prompt:
A feed team wants to predict whether a user will click a displayed post. Build a baseline and explain how you would evaluate and improve it.

Implement `predict_clicks(train_data, test_data)`. Each record contains numeric `hours_spent_reading_a`, `hours_spent_reading_b`, and `hours_spent_reading_c`, plus `current_post_category` (`A`, `B`, or `C`). Training records also contain the binary label `click`. Assume complete tabular data.

Return a dictionary with `predictions` (one 0/1 value per test record) and `metrics` containing `accuracy`, `f1_score`, and `roc_auc`. Explain which labeled split you use for those metrics, your treatment of the categorical feature, and the limits of a small baseline evaluation.

You may use pandas and scikit-learn, including a ready-made LogisticRegression model; implementing gradient descent from scratch is not required. Focus on inspecting the data, encoding the categorical feature, scaling numeric features, fitting preprocessing only on the training split, and evaluating the baseline. For the small executable fixture, metrics computed on train_data are training diagnostics, not evidence of generalization. A realistic evaluation needs a separate labeled validation split. The fixture training data contains both label classes.

Source boundary: the function signature, exact fields, and executable checks are a local practice reconstruction. The linked firsthand reports describe notebook data analysis and model training; they do not establish a NumPy-only restriction.
